objective: The exit proof's third run (2026-10-30 12:40) got a clean cross-provider review for the first time: Codex read the candidate and returned REJECT with two real MEDIUM findings, and the gatekeeper, now shown them, answered AMENDMENT_REQUIRED with a precise instruction. The loop then refused the correction: "the amendment named no path to correct". ProjectOS grants a correction worker only the files the amendment instruction names (pathsNamedIn, inside the phase's approved maximum), but nothing tells the gatekeeper so: its evidence pack says only "Edit(path) and Write(path) only", which it copied as the literal allowedActions "Edit(path)"; and the reviewer cited "validate-site.cjs:195" without its folder. This phase tells the gatekeeper, in the correctionMechanism part of its evidence, to name each file to correct by its full repository-relative path from workerWritableMaximum, and asks the reviewer to cite files by their repository-relative path. The correction boundary itself (protected) is unchanged: an amendment that names no permitted path is still refused. The exit proof runs after it. The ECC SECURITY review of this phase then showed a deeper gap: the production run command never supplies a correction maximum (always empty), and by design a correction maximum may not include the phase's own implementation files, so an independent reviewer's REJECT had no fix route at all and every rejection ended on the owner. Owner, 2026-10-30, verbatim: "Claude fixes, re-review (Recommended)" — on an independent rejection, the loop re-runs the same implementer with the reviewer's findings, writing only the files the plan already approved for the phase, up to the existing limit of three corrections, then re-runs the checks and obtains a fresh independent review. No new permission: the grant is the phase's own approved writePaths, re-issued for that one dispatch only; a rejection still never counts as a pass; when the budget is spent the run stops as before. The ECC SECURITY recheck accepted the route as an owner-authorised narrowing but required the protected rule BC-8n (val-projectos-boot-continue1a.cjs: "a correction dispatch never carries the implementer's write grant") to be reworded honestly before closure. Owner, 2026-10-30, verbatim: "Yes, reword it (Recommended)" — BC-8n states that a correction never carries the implementer's write grant EXCEPT the one dispatch right after an independent reviewer's rejection, limited to the phase's approved files and the existing three-attempt budget, as rule RC-1 checks; its check still fails if the grant reaches any other dispatch.
